[Shot 1]

Clip-local 0.00s–4.95s, KF1 → KF2: Begin exactly from the physical state established by KF1. Keep the same central hall axis and low viewing angle, then perform a smooth, slow forward dolly toward the high-backed throne. Use no cut, jump in scale, axis change, abrupt reframing, or unsupported initial blocking. Because KF1 supplies the starting body arrangement visually, allow only natural stabilization from that established arrangement into KF2 without crossing paths or exchanging positions. Maintain primary visual emphasis on <Subject 3> at frame left and <Subject 4> at frame right as both settle into upright postures facing <Subject 1>. <Subject 1> remains seated at the center of the elevated throne with an appraising gaze directed toward them. <Subject 2> remains beside the throne steps with hands lowered in front, respectful posture, restrained breathing, and stable balance. Complete the interval at the closer camera position and balanced left-right arrangement defined by KF2 while keeping all four Subjects spatially legible.

Clip-local 4.95s–13.00s, KF2 → KF3: Continue the same slow forward dolly along the unchanged central axis and low angle in one uninterrupted take. Preserve the throne and the left-right relationship of <Subject 3> and <Subject 4> in the same ensemble composition. During the later part of the interval, <Subject 4> remains on the right and raises both forearms in front of the body; the hands separate gradually to either side and rotate until both palms face upward, creating a clear supporting outline with empty space between them. No cloth, fabric, or other object materializes. <Subject 3> remains on the left and slowly inclines the body slightly toward <Subject 4> and the throne while retaining a composed expression. Do not pan away or track <Subject 4> independently. Arrive naturally at KF3, then hold that final canonical visual state only through Clip-local 13.10s without introducing any further action or story development.

The camera begins a smooth, slow advance on the central axis as <Subject 3> and <Subject 4> naturally rise from their bows without stepping or exchanging sides. A slight compositional balance toward frame left keeps <Subject 3>'s face and mouth readable beneath the wide brim while the others watch with relaxed closed lips. <Subject 3> (S1) says, <d>[Chinese] 尊贵的陛下。</d>

As <Subject 3>'s articulation ends, his lips settle closed and his attention turns toward his companion. The ensemble framing gently favors the right side enough to reveal <Subject 4>'s unobstructed face and mouth while <Subject 4> remains in his established place; <Subject 1>, <Subject 2>, and <Subject 3> listen with natural breathing, blinking, and closed mouths. <Subject 4> (S2) says, <d>[Chinese] 我们终于有幸见到您了。</d>

When <Subject 4> finishes, his mouth relaxes closed. The continuing central advance and a restrained compositional rebalance clear the foreground silhouettes and give the seated <Subject 1> a useful, readable face and mouth view without changing anyone's position. The visitors settle as attentive closed-mouth listeners. <Subject 1> (S3) asks, <d>[Chinese] 听说你们会织一种特别的布？</d>

After the emperor's lips close, a gentle leftward emphasis and exchanged gaze make <Subject 3>'s mouth readable in place; <Subject 1> remains seated, and the other listeners keep relaxed closed lips. <Subject 3> (S1) replies, <d>[Chinese] 是的，陛下。</d> As his reply ends, he closes his mouth and holds a composed expression. The camera recenters through the same continuous advance, restoring a clear view of the seated emperor while both visitors remain standing on their established sides. <Subject 1> (S3) asks, <d>[Chinese] 它有多漂亮？</d>

The emperor's articulation stops and his gaze begins to lower. Without walking forward, <Subject 4> remains at right as the framing and shared gaze make his face and mouth clearly readable; <Subject 1>, <Subject 2>, and <Subject 3> listen with closed mouths. <Subject 4> (S2) answers, <d>[Chinese] 它轻得像清晨的雾。</d> During the answer, he raises both forearms, gradually separates his empty hands, and turns both palms upward to suggest supporting ornate fabric while leaving only empty space between them.
